tagline: From an Ohio River boat town into the old coal hills.
intro: SR 78 leaves the Ohio River at Clarington, a river port where packet boats were once built at the mouth of Sunfish Creek, and turns west into the foothills of the Appalachians. It goes by way of Woodsfield and Caldwell, crosses the Muskingum at McConnelsville and finishes in Nelsonville. Along the south side of Burr Oak State Park the curves turn extreme, and locals sometimes call that stretch the Rim of the World.
Much of the way is old coal country. Ten thousand acres of it were stripped by a single machine and later reclaimed.

moments.title: Miners' Memorial Park
moments.text: When Big Muskie, a dragline 22 stories tall, was scrapped in 1999, its bucket was kept, and it rests here with room enough for two Greyhound buses side by side.

moments.title: Morgan County Dungeon
moments.text: From 1833 to 1839 McConnelsville held its convicted rioters, thieves and adulterers in this 11-foot-high cell, which came to light in 1964 when the ground was dug for the new sheriff's office.

moments.title: Nelsonville
moments.text: The road ends in Nelsonville, where many of the sidewalks on the public square are laid with glazed paving brick made from the valley's dense clay, some of it marked with a star.
